behavior: An aerial insectivore that hunts with quick wingbeats and short glides, usually low over water. Frequently perches between foraging flights. Territorial and often solitary or paired while breeding, but may join small flocks outside the breeding period. Nests in low natural or artificial cavities near water.
field_marks: Clean white throat, breast, and belly
Narrow white supraloral chevron above the black lores
Small black bill with dark eyes and short dark legs
Long, pointed blackish wings and a shallow-forked dark tail
habitat: Tropical lowlands around still or slow-moving open water, including mangrove forest, coastal lagoons, rivers, lakes, wetlands, and intertidal areas; nesting requires nearby cavities in trees, stumps, rocks, structures, or nest boxes.
